sit: Your goalie saves the puck to the corner. Two players from the other team skate toward it. You are the closest defender to your net.
opts: Skate to the front of your net and keep your stick on the ice
Chase both attackers deep into the corner
Stand behind your own net and wait
Skate up to the blue line for a pass
explain: The puck is in the corner, but the dangerous place is in front of your goalie. At U7, the simple read is to protect the net first.

sit: If a player on the other team has the puck behind your net, you should chase them around the back and leave the front of the net open.
why: They cannot score from behind the net. Stay near the front so you can stop a pass or loose puck by your goalie.

sit: Your teammate is skating down the side and is about to shoot. You are skating down the middle.
opts: Skate into the corner in case the puck misses
Stop near the side of the net with your stick on the ice for a rebound
Skate up to your teammate and crowd the puck
Stop high in the zone and watch
explain: Shots often bounce off the goalie. If you stop near the net with your stick ready, you can be first to the rebound.

sit: The other team steals the puck and skates fast toward your net. A defender stops at the center red line and watches them go by.
question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They stopped skating instead of coming back to help protect their net
They should have chased from behind with only their stick
They should have waited at the blue line for a pass
They should have stayed near the other team's net
explain: When the other team gets the puck, your job changes to defense. Skate back hard and help your goalie.

sit: You are standing in front of the other team's net. Your teammate has the puck in the corner and looks at you.
opts: Wave your hands while your stick is off the ice
Skate right up to your teammate and bring traffic with you
Keep your stick blade flat on the ice as a target
Turn your back and skate away from the net
explain: A good pass needs a clear target. Keeping your stick on the ice shows where the puck should go and gets you ready to shoot.

sit: You are skating down the ice with the puck. A defender is standing still in front of you. The side of the ice is empty.
opts: Put your head down and skate straight at the defender
Stop moving and wait for them to move away
Steer to the empty side and skate past them
Shoot the puck from far away before you get closer
explain: When someone blocks your path, look for open ice. Steering to the empty side is safer than skating into traffic.

sit: When you hear the referee blow the whistle, you should keep playing just in case the puck goes in.
why: The whistle means the play is stopped. Good players stop right away and get ready for the next play.

sit: You dig the puck out of the corner beside your own goalie. A defender is standing in front of your net.
opts: Skate the puck up the boards, keeping it close to the wall
Skate the puck right across the front of your own net
Leave the puck in the corner and skate away
Pass it backward toward your own goalie
explain: The front of your own net is dangerous. The boards are the safer path when you are leaving your zone.

sit: A player gets a pass in the middle of the ice. Only the goalie is between them and the net. They pass the puck backward right away.
question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They should have shot from farther away
They passed instead of skating toward the net to shoot
They should have skated into the corner to be safe
They should have waited until a defender caught them
explain: When you have open ice and a chance to score, keep your feet moving toward the net and shoot.

sit: You are on a breakaway with only the goalie in front of you. A player from the other team is skating hard behind you.
opts: Stop skating and let them catch up
Keep skating fast toward the net and shoot
Turn around and skate back toward the player chasing you
Shoot the puck into the corner and chase it
explain: On a breakaway, speed helps you stay ahead. Keep your feet moving and go to the net.

sit: You get the puck near the boards. A player from the other team skates at you. The ice along the wall is open.
opts: Keep your feet moving and skate up the boards into open ice
Stop skating and hide the puck between your skates
Pass across the front of your own net
Stand still and wait for help
explain: Open ice helps you escape. Keep moving into the space instead of stopping where pressure can catch you.

sit: If two of your teammates are already in the corner battling for the puck, you should skate into the same corner and stand beside them.
why: If two teammates are already near the puck, they need someone open. Move to space so they have a pass.

sit: You are skating with the puck, but it slips off your stick. It is only a few feet away.
opts: Keep skating in a big circle to come back for it
Give up and let the other team have it
Look at your stick before chasing the puck
Stop, turn, and get back on the puck
explain: Everyone loses the puck sometimes. Stop and turn right away so you can win it back.

sit: Your teammate has the puck on the boards. Two defenders are poking at them. You skate right up next to your teammate and stand still.
question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They joined the crowd instead of finding open ice
They should have poked the puck away from their teammate
They should have hidden behind the other team's net
They should have skated back to their own goalie
explain: If you stand in the same crowd, your teammate has no easy pass. Move to open ice and show your stick.

sit: You pick up a loose puck in the middle of the ice. Nobody is between you and the other team's goalie.
opts: Pass to a teammate who is covered
Carry the puck toward the net as fast as you can
Skate backward with the puck
Shoot from center ice right away
explain: When you have open ice, use it. Carrying the puck closer gives you a better chance to score.

sit: You are in the corner with the puck. A defender's stick blocks the direct pass, and your teammate is open nearby.
opts: Bank the puck softly off the boards to your teammate
Try to chop the puck through the defender's stick
Cover the puck with your hand
Shoot the puck high at the glass
explain: The boards can help you pass around a stick. A soft bank pass can reach your teammate when the straight pass is blocked.

sit: When a defender follows you around the back of the net, stopping and going back the other way can help you find open ice.
tip: Use the net as a shield.
why: The net can block the defender's path. A quick stop and turn can help you skate out the open side.

sit: You have the puck near your goal line. A forechecker is coming to trap you on the wall.
opts: Force the puck straight up the wall into pressure
Throw the puck blindly to the front of your own net
Fake up the boards, turn back, and skate behind your net
Stop on the wall and wait
explain: A simple fake can make space. Show one way, then turn to the open ice behind your net.
tip: Fake one way, go the other.

sit: A player picks up a loose puck in their defensive zone. A forechecker skates toward them, and the player smacks the puck into a crowded corner.
question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They panicked and threw the puck away instead of skating to open ice
They should have passed through the forechecker's skates
They should have skated into their goalie
They should have shot from their own zone
explain: When pressure comes, do not throw the puck away. Use your feet to turn toward open ice and keep the puck safer.

sit: A defender slides on the ice in front of you to block your shot.
opts: Shoot right into the defender's pads
Pull the puck around them and shoot through the open lane
Pass backward right away even though you can shoot
Leave the puck and skate away
explain: When a defender slides down, they cannot turn quickly. Pull the puck around them and use the open lane.

sit: You are backchecking hard through the middle. The puck carrier is skating down the wing, and your defenseman has a good angle on them. Another opponent is driving straight toward your net.
opts: Chase the puck carrier and leave the middle open
Pick up the player driving the net and take away their stick
Stop skating once you cross your blue line
Drift behind your own net and wait for the puck
explain: Read the biggest threat. If your defenseman has the puck carrier angled, the open player going to the net is more dangerous. Cover that player first.

sit: When you are defending a 2-on-1, you should rush straight at the puck carrier and leave the pass option open.
why: On a 2-on-1, the goalie can handle the shot better if the defender protects the middle and takes away the dangerous pass.

sit: Your team is cycling the puck low in the corner. You are the high forward (F3). You see the defense has collapsed below the faceoff dots.
opts: Join the crowded corner battle
Back all the way out to the red line
Slide into the open high slot, show your stick, and stay ready to recover
Stand beside the goalie and wait for a rebound
explain: F3 can use the space the defense gives up, but still has to stay responsible. The high slot is open, and you are still above the puck if possession changes.
tip: Find quiet ice above the puck.

sit: A center takes a defensive-zone faceoff. They win the puck cleanly to their defenseman, but instead of tying up the opposing center, they skate away toward the blue line.
question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They should have tried to shoot off the draw
They failed to tie up their check, giving the opposing center a free path to the net
They should have chased their own defenseman for the puck
They should have left the circle before the puck was dropped
explain: Winning the draw is only the first job. In the defensive zone, the center still has to stop their check from getting to the net.

sit: Your defenseman shoots from the point. The goalie kicks a rebound into the low slot and is down away from the puck.
opts: Take a big wind-up before shooting
Stop hard, keep your stick on the ice, and shoot quickly
Pass the puck back to the point to reset
Carry the puck behind the net for a wraparound
explain: A loose rebound near the net is a quick-play chance. When the goalie is down and away from the puck, shoot quickly before defenders recover.

sit: You are a defenseman at the offensive blue line. You catch a pass, but two defenders are blocking the lane to the net. Your center is open in the corner.
opts: Shoot into the defenders' shin pads
Hold the puck at the blue line until pressure reaches you
Pass down to your open center to keep possession
Stickhandle into the crowded high slot
explain: A blocked point shot can turn into a rush against you. If the shooting lane is closed, move the puck to an open teammate and keep the play alive.

sit: When leading a 3-on-2 rush, the best decision is always to dump the puck into the corner.
why: A 3-on-2 gives your team an advantage. Carry or pass to make the defenders choose, instead of giving the puck away automatically.

sit: You recover a loose puck below your own goal line. Two forecheckers are closing from one side, but your winger is open on the far boards with a clear lane.
opts: Try to stickhandle through both forecheckers
Pass firmly to your open winger on the far boards
Rim the puck hard without checking the lane
Skate the puck across the front of your own net
explain: Pressure on one side usually opens space somewhere else. A firm pass to the open winger moves the puck away from danger and starts the breakout.

sit: A player receives a pass in the offensive slot with a clear lane to the net. Instead of shooting, they force a backhand pass to a covered teammate back door.
question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They should have held the puck longer to draw more defenders
They passed up a strong scoring chance to force a low-percentage pass
They should have dumped the puck into the corner
They should have skated away from the slot first
explain: In the slot, a clear shooting lane is a great chance. Forcing a pass to a covered teammate gives the defense time to recover.

sit: You are the last defender back. An opposing player skates at you 1-on-1 with speed and tries to push the puck wide.
opts: Turn your hips, keep your body between them and the net, and steer them to the boards
Dive forward and hope your stick reaches the puck
Skate straight at them and guess which way they will go
Stop skating and reach with one hand
explain: The last defender protects the middle first. If you dive or guess, you can give up a clean chance. Angle the puck carrier toward the boards.

sit: You receive a breakout pass in the neutral zone. The opposing defenseman steps up quickly to close your space. Your teammate is skating past them along the boards.
opts: Try to toe-drag through the defender's stick
Chip the puck softly into the space behind the defenseman for your teammate
Stop moving and let the pressure reach you
Shoot the puck high around the glass with no target
explain: When a defender steps up, they leave space behind them. A soft chip lets your teammate skate onto the puck with speed.

sit: When you have the puck in the offensive zone and the middle is open, skating into a crowded corner is the best way to create space.
why: Corners can protect the puck, but they are not the best choice when the middle is open. Moving or passing toward open ice creates more danger.

sit: Your defenseman has the puck in your zone. The other team's wingers are covering the boards and taking away the easy wall pass.
opts: Stand on the boards anyway and call for the puck
Skate down beside your own goal line and crowd your defenseman
Cut through the middle to give your defenseman a clear passing option
Skate into the offensive zone and wait for a long pass
explain: If the boards are covered, the middle may be open. Cutting through the middle gives your defenseman a useful passing option.

sit: A player carries the puck up the wing. A defender has a tight gap and matches their speed. Instead of passing, chipping, or delaying, the player tries to skate straight through the defender.
question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They did not recognize that the defender had taken away their space
They should have shot from the red line
They should have skated backward into the neutral zone
They should have stopped and waited on the boards
explain: When a defender matches your speed and closes your space, forcing the puck through them is low percentage. Pass, chip, or delay for support.

sit: You are regrouping in the neutral zone with the puck. The other team is changing lines, giving you open ice in front of you.
opts: Pass the puck backward right away to slow the game down
Dump the puck in even though the defenders are not set
Attack the open space with speed before they organize
Stop skating and wait for the new players to get on the ice
explain: A line change can create time and space. Attacking quickly forces the other team to defend before they are set.

sit: You pick up a loose puck in your own corner. A forechecker is coming fast from the goal line and trying to trap you on the boards.
opts: Force the puck straight up the wall into the forechecker's stick
Throw the puck blindly to the front of your own net
Fake up the boards, pull the puck back, and skate behind your net
Stop on the wall and wait for pressure
explain: A simple fake can create your own space. Showing up the wall can freeze the forechecker long enough for you to escape behind the net.

sit: If a defender has you pinned on the boards, the best move is always to hack the puck forward into their skates.
why: Hacking forward usually gives the puck away. Under pressure, protect it and use a support option, like kicking or nudging it back to a teammate.

sit: You enter the offensive zone 1-on-1. The defender has a tight gap and takes away your path to the net.
opts: Shoot directly into the defender's pads
Slow up, protect the puck, and wait for a teammate to become a late option
Push the puck through the defender's skates
Turn all the way back to the center red line
explain: When the first option is gone, a delay can create a new one. Slowing up gives support time to arrive and keeps possession.

sit: A player receives a pass in the high slot but a defender drops down to block the lane. Instead of changing the angle, the player shoots directly into the defender.
question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They did not pull the puck to the side to open a clear shooting lane
They used a wrist shot instead of a slapshot
They should have dumped the puck into the corner
They should have passed backward out of the zone
explain: When a defender goes down, they cannot adjust quickly. A small drag or side-step can open a cleaner lane to the net.

sit: You are pressured on the half-wall. You saw your center open in the slot, but the direct passing lane is blocked and you cannot turn for a forehand pass.
opts: Hold the puck until the pressure takes it away
Throw a blind backhand pass through the defender
Bank the puck off the boards so it angles toward your open center
Spin into the pressure before making a pass
explain: A direct pass is blocked, but the boards can create a new lane. An indirect pass works when you know your teammate is open and can angle the puck to them.
